direction.premise: A cooperative falling-block arcade rebuilt around a legible single shared well, even on narrow phones.
direction.composition: A light editorial entry becomes a high-contrast centered well with compact score to the side or above, next pieces on a rail, and an ergonomic two-thumb control deck.
direction.shapeLanguage: Crisp square stack cells, quiet linear menu rows, pill-free directional keys and one heavy color-filled hard-drop key.
direction.surfaceAndMaterial: Warm paper shell and sage hardware borders surround a dark deep-green playing well; no glass overlays, purple gradients or neon chromed cabinet.
direction.paletteLogic: A neutral matte shell yields attention to player-owned cyan, pink, yellow and green cells; the hard-drop key is deep green.
direction.typography: Humanist sans for mode choices, tightly-spaced monospace for score and technical status; labels stay concise.
direction.signature: The multiplayer phone well expands to full width automatically, while the two-thumb deck supports both precise hold controls and direct canvas swipe rotation.
direction.distinction: Distinct from ZAMAZKA's art paper and FOG's tactical maps: this is a fitted precision arcade well within a restrained editorial instrument, not a decorative game cabinet.

architecture.primaryVerb: Place falling pieces into the one shared well: hold horizontal movement or soft-drop, rotate with a tap, swipe in whole-cell steps, or hard-drop.
architecture.physicalFeedback: Two-thumb buttons depress by 3px on pointer contact, local gestures resolve immediately, online snapshots reconcile to the authoritative well.
architecture.spatialRationale: The smallest screen reserves the most area for its current 20-row field, shifts wide shared wells to full-width play, and keeps two control groups at thumb reach; landscape moves controls left of the well.

comparisons.spatialDifference: The perekos layout differs from Blockies: warm outer shell, full-width shared grid on phones, tiny numeric strip and two-thumb input deck.
comparisons.interactionDifference: Blockies requires cell-precise hold, canvas swipe and fast hard drop, with PocketNet authoritative shared state instead of perekos interaction.

comparisons.spatialDifference: Black Bazaar emphasizes collections and marketplace information panels; Blockies retains one unbroken, center-weighted 20-row play well, a slim score rail, and a thumb-reachable control deck.
comparisons.interactionDifference: Trade decisions and inventory inspection do not translate into the one-cell, continuous gravity-based movement, rotation and instant hard drop required by Blockies.

comparisons.spatialDifference: Picto arranges communal symbol and clue slots for group interpretation, while Blockies gives the falling board priority and moves its reward register into an optional overlay away from active play.
comparisons.interactionDifference: Picto's deliberate simultaneous symbol choices differ from Blockies' real-time movement with repeat-on-hold controls and server-verified collaborative line clears.

production.renderer: Canvas 2D paints crisp, flat tiles with light rims and ghost landings; source collision, scoring, seeded pieces and server-authoritative online rules are preserved.
production.focalAsset: Dark 20-row well and shared bright tetromino silhouettes; matte stack-shaped SVG install identity matches the new shell.

motion.character: Gravity, directional repeat and swipe displacement use visible cell-by-cell changes, never interpolation that misrepresents landing coordinates.
motion.action: Move and rotate your own falling piece, then drop it into the shared stack while leaving room for the other player.
motion.anticipation: A ghost silhouette, next piece rail and legible room ready indicators prepare the next exact move.
motion.response: A key depresses on touch, then the piece moves or rotates; hard drop snaps to the ghost position; server snapshots remain authoritative.
motion.followThrough: Line-clear bonuses enter the compact feed without covering the well; score updates pulse once.
motion.interruption: Pointer cancel, disconnect and app background release held controls; room rejoin restores authoritative state.
motion.reducedMotion: Prefer-reduced-motion strips UI transitions without affecting Tetris gravity or button/input semantics.

evidence.expectedChange: Mode selection opens the 20-row shared board with crisp cells, a next-piece rail and independent direction/rotation/hard-drop controls fitted to the viewport.
